name: White City of Tel-Aviv – the Modern Movement
description: In the heart of Tel Aviv, Israel, the White City is a district of more than 4,000 buildings from the 1930s to 1950s, in the clean-lined style often called Bauhaus. Architects trained in Europe, many of them Jewish refugees from Nazi Germany, designed them to suit a hot Mediterranean climate. Streets laid out on a plan by Patrick Geddes make it ideal for wandering on foot.
